title: else
goal: In this lesson you will learn how else runs when the if condition is False.
learn: Run one path or the other
idea: else is the backup plan. It runs only when the if condition is False. Write else: at the same indent as if, then indent the else block. Exactly one of the two blocks runs. Never both, never neither (for a simple if/else).
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change score = 55 to score = 85. Press Run. You should see You passed! instead.

practice.text: If age is at least 12, print Teen ticket. Else print Kid ticket. Set age to 10.
practice.hint: Use if age >= 12: for the first message, then else: at the same indent as if for the backup. Indent each print under its line.
practice.starterTip: With age 10, the if fails. So the else block should print Kid ticket.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if else path prints Kid ticket for age 10.

practice.text: Set found = True. If found, print Key found, else print Keep looking.
practice.hint: A bool variable can go straight in the if: if found: means “if found is True.” Pair it with else: for the other message.
practice.starterTip: After found = True, write if/else with indented prints. You should see Key found because found is True.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if if/else prints Key found when found is True.

quiz.question: When does else run?
quiz.wrong: else runs only if the if condition failed.

quiz.question: Does else need its own condition?
quiz.wrong: else has no condition; if already asked the question.

quiz.question: Can if and else both print in one run of a simple if/else?
quiz.correct: Exactly one of the two blocks runs.
quiz.wrong: They are alternatives: one path only.
